title: Retire `PluginComponentInput` stage 2 — delete the deprecated alias (and the now-dead `plugin-scope.ts` re-export feeding it)
body:
Stage 2 of the two-stage retirement the maintainer ruled on 2026-08-22 (parent #5674, item 13 = A: *"mark the alias `@deprecated` pointing at `ComponentInput` for one release, then remove"*).

Stage 1 shipped the deprecation. This card is the removal half, and it is **deliberately not ready to dispatch yet** — see *When* below.

## What to remove

Two lines, both in `@object-ui/types`:

1. `packages/types/src/index.ts` — the `ComponentInput as PluginComponentInput,` specifier and the `@deprecated` JSDoc block above it.
2. `packages/types/src/plugin-scope.ts` — the `export type { ComponentInput } from './base.js';` re-export.

The second one is easy to miss and is the reason it is written down here. It is a **separate binding** from the `import type { ComponentInput } from './base.js'` at the top of the same file. The *import* types `ComponentMeta.inputs` and must stay. The *re-export* has exactly one consumer — the aliased specifier in `index.ts` — so it goes dead the moment (1) is deleted. A comment in `plugin-scope.ts` says so at the site.

Also delete, or convert, `packages/types/src/__tests__/plugin-component-input-deprecation.test.ts`: it pins *"deprecated, not removed"*, so it is designed to go red when this card lands. That is the pin doing its job, not a regression. Removing the subject removes the pin with it — the same disposition `cloud-environment-vocabulary.pin.test.ts` got when its subject was deleted.

## Bump

`minor`, with a **FROM → TO** breaking block in the changeset naming exactly what is no longer exported — the shape both prior published-export removals in this repo used (`@object-ui/data-objectstack`, `CloudOperations` and the four-module removal). Never `major`: this repo's own breaking changes track `@objectstack`'s major, they do not set it.

No compile-compat stub. Same reasoning both precedents record: with no consumer to keep compiling, a stub is a second phantom surface guarding the first.

## When

**Not before a release actually ships the stage-1 deprecation.** The window is the entire point of the two-stage ruling: in-repo the name has zero importers (measured across every root plus the sibling framework repo, with a control), but what cannot be measured from inside this repository is an importer on npm — and that is the claim that licenses deleting an export from a published package. Deleting before the deprecation has shipped gives outside consumers a silent break, which is exactly what the ruling declined to do.

Before landing, re-run the zero-importer measurement rather than trusting this card: it is a claim about the world at filing time.

## Verify

`node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` · `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` · `check-changeset-fixed.mjs` · `pnpm --filter '@object-ui/types' type-check` · `pnpm vitest run --project unit packages/types/` · rebuild and diff the emitted `dist/index.d.ts` so the published surface change is shown, not inferred.
